newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says deputies back his plan to fill holes.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says deputies back his plan to fill holes.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said the Christian Democrats (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) unanimously approved his proposal to fill budget holes with stepped up privatisation of government holdings.

The ruling coalition of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's CDU/CSU alliance and liberal Free Democrats will now debate the government's plans with opposition parties in a special session of parliament on Friday.

Waigel said the CDU/CSU parliamentary group also approved his intention to draw up legislation, which he hopes to pass by the summer, that would enable the Bundesbank to raise the value of its gold and foreign exchange reserves.
The Bundesbank currently books its assets at their all-time lowest price or at the purchase price, a method which is normal under German book-keeping regulations.

A revaluation would effectively deliver Bonn a windfall profit, allowing it to retire old debt more quickly than otherwise. But Waigel played down this aspect of the changes, selling it instead as a technical move to prepare for the euro currency.
Waigel said the revaluation of the gold would not contribute to the reduction of the current deficit, but would help German fulfill the criteria for a single European currency.

Waigel said he told the meeting of lawmakers that the government was counting on "stepped up privatisations" to offset a shortfall in tax revenues that is forecast at 18 billion marks ($10.6 billion) below previous estimates that formed the basis of the government's 1997 budget.
